title: Reduced rational homology of the proper interval in a product of finite chains
statement: Let $r\geq1$ and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbf N^r$ be nonzero. Order $[0,m]=\prod_{i=1}^r\{0,\ldots,m_i\}$ coordinatewise, and let $T_m=[0,m]\setminus\{0,m\}$. Define an augmented chain complex $A(m)$ of rational vector spaces [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] as follows. For $k\geq0$, its basis consists of strict chains $v_0<\cdots<v_k$ in $T_m$; $A(m)_{-1}=\mathbf Q$ on the empty chain, and $A(m)_k=0$ for $k<-1$. The differential for $k\geq1$ deletes one vertex with signs $\sum_{a=0}^k(-1)^a[v_0<\cdots<\widehat v_a<\cdots<v_k]$; the degree-zero differential sends every vertex to $1\in\mathbf Q$, and the degree $-1$ differential is zero. If at least one $m_i\geq2$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for every integer $k$. If every $m_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $s=\#\{i:m_i=1\}$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for $k\ne s-2$ and $\dim_{\mathbf Q}H_{s-2}(A(m))=1$. This includes $s=1$, when $T_m$ is empty and the nonzero homology is in degree $-1$.

proof.text: Identify $A(m)$ with $C(T_m;\mathbf Q)$ [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains] by sending each strict-chain basis vector to the identical list basis vector and the empty generator to the empty generator. The inverse sends those lists back; both commute with alternating deletion and augmentation, and lower terms are zero. If $m_j\geq2$, [lem-sfb-product-interval-nullhomotopy] supplies $dt+td=\operatorname{id}$ for $R=\mathbf Q$. For any cycle $z$ in any integer degree this gives $z=d(tz)$, hence its class in $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] is zero. This proves the non-Boolean clause.

proof.text: Suppose every $m_i\in\{0,1\}$. Put $E=\{i:m_i=1\}$ and $s=|E|\geq1$, since $m\ne0$. Send a vector $x\leq m$ to $\{i:x_i=1\}$, with inverse the indicator vector; this order bijection identifies $T_m$ with $P_E=\{S:\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq E\}$. On strict-chain bases and the empty chain the two inverse maps commute with every deletion; they therefore induce inverse maps on kernels modulo images, giving $A(m)\cong B_E=C(P_E;\mathbf Q)$ [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]. Induct on $s$ with the claim for every finite set $E$ of size $s$. If $s=1$, the poset is empty, so $B_E$ is $\mathbf Q$ in degree $-1$ and zero otherwise, with zero differentials. Its homology is $\mathbf Q$ in degree $-1=s-2$ and zero elsewhere by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: For $s\geq2$ choose $a\in E$ and set $v=E\setminus\{a\}$, so $|v|=s-1\geq1$. Use the quotient-induced derived isomorphism of [lem-sfb-boolean-coatom-excision-derived], whose per-degree consequence [lem-sfb-boolean-coatom-excision-homology] is $H_n(B_E)\cong H_{n-1}(B_v)$ for every integer $n$. The induction hypothesis for $v$ says the latter vanishes unless $n-1=(s-1)-2=s-3$, equivalently $n=s-2$, and has dimension one there. For $s=2$ this uses the singleton base case in degree $n-1=-1$, hence gives the nonzero group in degree $n=0$; for every $s$ the isomorphism preserves zero spaces and dimensions in all integer degrees. This proves the inductive step. The chain identification of step 2 proves the Boolean clause with arbitrary zero coordinates, and step 1 supplies all remaining cases: a natural coordinate outside $\{0,1\}$ is at least $2$.
